newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico H1 direct foreign investment $1.495 bln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico H1 direct foreign investment $1.495 bln.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Mexico in the first six months of the year, registered by the government as of July 24, was $1.495 billion, the Trade Ministry said Monday.

The ministry said that taking into account net imports of fixed assets by maquiladora (in-bond assembly for export) plants worth $40.5 million, direct foreign investment totalled $1.945 billion in the first half of the year.
It gave no comparative figures for the first half of last year.

The ministry said that it received information in June about direct foreign investment worth $941.8 million, of which $865.5 million was registered with the National Register of Foreign Investment. It said that $76.3 million of the June total consisted of maquiladora purchases of fixed assets from abroad.
Of the total reported to the National Register in June, the ministry said 30.1 percent or $260.3 million was invested before 1996 and 69.9 percent or $605.2 million between January and May this year.

The difference between the date of registration and the date of investment is due to the fact that investors do not go immediately to the National Registry once their investments have been made, the ministry said.

Of the $941.8 million in investment of which the ministry was notified in June, 80.9 percent or $762.1 million went to the industrial sector, 14.7 percent $138.3 million to trade, 2.2 percent or $20.5 million to community, social and personal services and 2.0 percent or $18.8 million to financial services.
The $76.3 million of foreign investment reported as having been made in June would go up in coming months as other investments were registered, it said.

The ministry said $628.8 million or 66.8 percent of the total investment notified to the ministry in June came from the United States, $238.1 million or 25.3 percent from India, $27.7 million or 2.9 percent from Japan and $22.2 million or 2.3 percent from France.

It added that in June seven private investment projects worth a total $128.8 million were approved, of which three were for professional services firms, two for manufacturing firms and two for construction firms.
